linkedin.hook: Eliminating pooled contagion risk in leveraged Soroban credit markets.
linkedin.copy:
Most lending protocols treat leverage as an internal pool problem. When traders loop interest-bearing collateral, the tail risk of bad debt sits directly on passive depositors. Blend v2 formal verification provides robust base primitives, but scaling capital efficiency requires isolating leveraged execution outside the core liquidity layer.

Vanna handles this through modular SmartAccounts on Soroban. By routing positions through isolated execution contracts that hold Blend b-tokens, leverage scales up to 10x while maintaining an invariant 1.10x Health Factor floor. Counterparty risk remains quarantined within individual contract boundaries rather than diffusing across shared liquidity pools.

On Stellar, execution throughput matters as much as formal safety guarantees. With 0.00014 XLM fixed gas overhead and ~320ms Mercury indexer latency, off-chain liquidators evaluate health vectors deterministically without network congestion bottlenecks. You can evaluate and deploy testnet SmartAccount instances at test.stellar.vanna.finance.

Institutional architecture is documented at test.stellar.vanna.finance

reddit.hook: How we built isolated 10x leverage on top of Blend v2 b-tokens without shared pool contagion
reddit.copy:
Shared pool lending models on Soroban typically break down when users aggressively loop derivative assets like b-tokens. If a high-volatility event hits, liquidators race for shared exits, and any systemic slip creates bad debt for passive lenders.

We approached this by designing Vanna SmartAccounts as sandboxed proxy contracts deployed on Soroban. Instead of opening a leveraged position directly against Blend, the user spins up an isolated SmartAccount that holds the collateral, borrows against it, and re-deposits the b-tokens in automated atomic transactions.

The core risk parameter is the 1.10x Health Factor floor. Because state transitions occur within individual Soroban storage spaces, liquidation logic can execute without scanning entire pool state trees. Gas consumption sits at roughly 0.00014 XLM per operation, and state synchronization relies on ~320ms Mercury indexer latency. If an account drops below the 1.10x floor, only that specific sandbox faces liquidation. Zero bad debt spills into Blend core pools or other SmartAccount instances.

You can test this architecture on testnet today. Point your wallet to test.stellar.vanna.finance, fund your address with testnet XLM, and invoke the factory contract to generate a sandbox SmartAccount.

Disclosure: I am a core engineer building Vanna Protocol.
